subject: Food Science
title: Whole Genome Sequencing
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Whole Genome Sequencing.

hook.text: In 2018, genomic sequencing linked a Listeria outbreak across 4 countries to a single factory in South Africa.

buildup.text: Whole genome sequencing (WGS) reads every letter of a bacterium's DNA—creating a unique genetic fingerprint.

discovery.text: WGS can match patient isolates to food samples with near certainty. Outbreaks are traced in days instead of weeks.

twist.text: Better detection finds more outbreaks—not more outbreaks occurring. It looks worse but means better surveillance.

climax.text: The FDA's GenomeTrakr network has sequenced over 500,000 isolates—the largest pathogen database in the world.

punchline.text: Every bacterium has a DNA fingerprint. Now we can read it and trace it back.

quiz.question: How does whole genome sequencing help in food safety?
options: It matches pathogen DNA from patients to food sources, tracing outbreaks rapidly
